chapter: Reel 2-3: tunes, closing and country life
title: Dog and rooster fights in the country
summary: Mrs. Clementin describes cockfights and dog fights in the country and Allen asks about fights on Oak Street and Southport.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I didn't have a cellar bag. No. I didn't have a cellar bag. I didn't have all kinds of tricks right there in the country. People used to have a best time. And they sent it... My brother was saying, wait, who used to fight? You know? We used to have them. We used to train to fight. We used to have that over there. And sometimes... We used to all fight. Yeah.
We used to have a dog. No, no.

She's talking about dogs. Yeah. On the country there, they had a little dog that they used to have. We had a dog. We had a dog. We talked about the dog. The smaller. Yeah. We used to have dogs. I had a dog. Yeah. But the dog in there, them cron. Of course. Huh? Dog in there, them cron. They can't say, the dog cron. Dog what? Cron. I thought she was asked about the dog cron. Clon. But the poor second one kind of slain. You'd have a dog to climb up a post? They had a post cron, you know. And then the dog would go, sir, this thing. They watch, watch. Then we got two for that to jump in the middle. You had a trainer. And then they used to send and get different women racerops to the fight.
